allowed_dependency_manifest.content: For each integer n at least 2, among all length n minus 1 sequences of plus or minus 1, determine exactly which sign patterns maximize the number of permutations of 1 through n whose consecutive differences have the prescribed signs.

forbidden_claims.statement_nl: Let $n$ be an integer with $n \\geq 2$. For a sequence $s = (s_1,\\dots,s_{n-1})$ where each $s_i = \\pm 1$, let $f(s)$ be the number of permutations $(a_1,\\dots,a_n)$ of $\\{1,2,\\dots,n\\}$ such that $s_i(a_{i+1}-a_i) > 0$ for all $i$. For each $n$, determine the sequences $s$ for which $f(s)$ is maximal.

statement_nl: Let n be an integer at least 2, and let s=(s_1,...,s_{n-1}) with each s_i in {+1,-1}. Define -s=(-s_1,...,-s_{n-1}). Let f(s) be the number of permutations a=(a_1,...,a_n) of {1,...,n} such that s_i(a_{i+1}-a_i)>0 for every 1 <= i <= n-1. Then f(s)=f(-s).
